# Chronological Account: Gemini 3 Pro Preview on `email-paper-homepage` (Toolathlon)

## The task

Index 22 in `gemini-3-pro-preview_1.jsonl` (`task_name: email-paper-homepage`). The run started 2025-11-21 15:11:59 and completed 2025-11-21 15:20:03. Per `task_status`, preprocessing finished, the agent ran to completion (not max-turn-exceeded), and `evaluation` returned `false`. Key stats: 1 user turn, 31 assistant turns, 34 tool calls, 100 messages, no truncations.

The single user message was:

> Update my personal homepage according to the following rules:
> - For papers currently marked as "preprint" or "under review" on my homepage, update their acceptance information according to my emails.
> - Update the status of code open-sourcing for these accepted papers only. If there is a released repository on my GitHub for the corresponding paper, update it on my homepage.

The agent had 128 tools available, including a GitHub MCP server (with allowed repos restricted to `My-Homepage,enhancing-llms,ipsum-lorem-all-you-need,llm-adaptive-learning,optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning`) and an Emails MCP. Single-turn mode was enabled with `max_steps_under_single_turn_mode: 100`. The system prompt told the agent to either call `local-claim_done` or respond without a tool call to terminate.

## Phase 1 — Disoriented opening (msgs 1–14)

The agent's very first call was a blind guess: `github-get_file_contents({"repo": "homepage", "owner": "my-personal-website"})` with no `path`. The server replied `"missing required parameter: path"`.

It then tried `github-list_repositories({"query": "user:me"})` — the tool does not exist (`"Tool github-list_repositories not found in agent Assistant"`).

Next it tried `github-search_repositories({"query": "user:test-user homepage"})` — guessing the username. GitHub returned a 422 Validation Failed.

Only on its 4th call did the agent run `github-get_me({})`, which returned `login: "toolathlon-testuser"`, 8 public repos. It then tried `github-list_repositories` again (still nonexistent), and finally on the 6th call ran `github-search_repositories({"query": "user:toolathlon-testuser"})`, which returned 6 repos: `My-Homepage`, `enhancing-llms`, `llm-adaptive-learning`, `LUFFY`, `optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning`, `ipsum-lorem-all-you-need`.

## Phase 2 — Repeated path-parameter errors (msgs 13–24)

The agent then tried 7 separate `github-get_file_contents` calls fishing for the right path:

- `path: ""` → "missing required parameter: path"
- `path: "index.html"` → 404
- `path: "README.md"` → returned the Academic Pages template README (giving Jekyll-template structural hints)
- `path: ""` (again) → "missing required parameter: path"
- `path: "_publications"` → `"file content SHA is nil"`
- `path: "_pages/publications.md"` → 404
- `path: "publications.md"` → 404

It then tried two `github-search_code` queries against the repo for "preprint" and "under review" (both returned `total_count: 0`, likely because GitHub had not yet indexed the brand-new repository).

Finally it fetched `_config.yml` (revealing "John Smith" as the homepage owner), tried an empty-path call once more (error), then tried `path: "/"` which finally returned the root directory listing. From there it called `path: "_publications"` (error again) then `path: "_publications/"` (with trailing slash) which returned the file list.

## Phase 3 — Reading the publication files (msgs 41–48)

The agent issued two parallel batches of three `github-get_file_contents` calls each, fetching six publication markdown files. The state on disk:

| File | Venue (existing) | codeurl (existing) |
|---|---|---|
| 2024-05-15-enhancing-llms.md | "Proceedings of … ACL 2024" | absent |
| 2025-01-10-ethical-llms.md | "… NeurIPS 2024" | absent |
| 2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md | "Under review at COML 2025 …" | absent |
| 2025-06-15-ipsum-lorem-workshop.md | "Under review at COML Workshop … (COMLW 2025)" | absent |
| 2025-06-20-llm-adaptive-learning.md | "Accepted at ICML 2025 …" | `https://github.com/mcptest-user/llm-adaptive-learning` (wrong username) |
| 2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md | "Under review at COAI 2025 …" | absent |

## Phase 4 — Email triage (msgs 49–58)

The agent only used the emails server in 4 calls, and only searched for two specific venue strings:

1. `emails-search_emails({"query": "COML 2025"})` → 7 hits (IDs 15, 14, 12, 8, 5, 2, 1: deadline reminders, registration confirmation, video-recording reminder, oral notification, COMLW camera-ready, COML camera-ready instructions). The agent opened only 2 of these 7:
   - **Email 5** — `[COML 2025] Oral presentation notification` — "your submission **Ipsum Lorem is all you need** has been selected for an oral presentation at COML 2025."
   - **Email 2** — `[COMLW 2025] Urgent: Camera-Ready Deadline Tomorrow` — "your paper titled 'Ipsum Lorem is all you need for a workshop'" implicitly accepted (camera-ready stage).
2. `emails-search_emails({"query": "COAI 2025"})` → 1 hit. The agent opened it:
   - **Email 16** — `[COAI 2025] Camera-Ready Instructions for Accepted Papers` — "Congratulations on your paper 'Optimizing Large Language Models for Contextual Reasoning in Multi-Task Environments' acceptance to … (COAI 2025)!"

The agent did NOT list folders, did not look at INBOX broadly, did not read the other 5 COML-related emails (IDs 15, 14, 12, 8, 1), and did not investigate whether other papers (e.g., `enhancing-llms`, `llm-adaptive-learning`) had related correspondence.

## Phase 5 — Verifying repository "release status" (NOT DONE)

Crucially, the agent **never inspected the contents** of any of the four code repos to determine whether they were "released and finished." It did not fetch their READMEs, list their commits, or check release tags. The only information it ever had about the repos was the bare metadata from the user-level `search_repositories` result (each had `stargazers_count: 0, forks_count: 0, open_issues_count: 0, archived: false`). Despite the README and evaluator both specifying that repos must be **verified** as released, the agent treated mere existence as proof of release.

## Phase 6 — Three sequential file writes (msgs 59–64)

The agent issued three `github-create_or_update_file` calls, one per assistant turn, each touching one publication file on the `master` branch:

**Write 1** — `_publications/2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md`
- `venue` changed to `'Accepted at COML 2025 - Conference on Machine Learning (Oral)'`
- `codeurl` ADDED: `'https://github.com/toolathlon-testuser/ipsum-lorem-all-you-need'`
- Commit message: "Update status to Accepted at COML 2025 and add code link"
- API returned 200 with new SHA.

**Write 2** — `_publications/2025-06-15-ipsum-lorem-workshop.md`
- `venue` changed to `'Accepted at COML Workshop on Large Language Models (COMLW 2025)'`
- No `codeurl` added.
- Commit message: "Update status to Accepted at COMLW 2025"
- API returned 200.

**Write 3** — `_publications/2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md`
- `venue` changed to `'Accepted at COAI 2025 - Conference on Artificial Intelligence'`
- `codeurl` ADDED: `'https://github.com/toolathlon-testuser/optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning'`
- Commit message: "Update status to Accepted at COAI 2025 and add code link"
- API returned 200.

## Phase 7 — Termination (msg 65)

The agent's final message contained no further tool calls — it returned a natural-language summary, which under the task's stop condition ends the task. The summary said:

1. Ipsum Lorem: updated to "Accepted at COML 2025 …" and added the `ipsum-lorem-all-you-need` codeurl.
2. Ipsum Lorem workshop: updated to "Accepted at COMLW 2025"; "No specific repository found for this workshop paper, so no code link was added (consistent with the instruction to only update if a released repository exists)."
3. Optimizing LLMs: updated to "Accepted at COAI 2025 …" and added `optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning` codeurl.
4. "The paper 'Adaptive Learning Strategies …' was already marked as accepted and had a code link, so it was left unchanged."

## What the evaluator was checking (per `evaluation/main.py`)

The evaluator runs three checks:

1. **`check_acceptance`** on the three previously-under-review files: each `venue` must contain "COML 2025", "COMLW 2025", "COAI 2025" respectively (case-insensitive) and must not contain "preprint" or "under review."
2. **`check_paper_repositories_codeurl`** on four files:
   - `2024-05-15-enhancing-llms.md` — MUST have `codeurl: https://github.com/{user}/enhancing-llms` (status "released").
   - `2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md` — MUST have `codeurl: https://github.com/{user}/ipsum-lorem-all-you-need` (status "released").
   - `2025-06-20-llm-adaptive-learning.md` — MUST have `codeurl: https://github.com/{user}/llm-adaptive-learning` (status "released").
   - `2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md` — MUST NOT have a `codeurl` (status "to_be_released" — the repo's README is annotated "🚧 To be released" in the evaluator's comment).
3. **`check_modified_files`** — only `_publications/2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md`, `_publications/2025-06-15-ipsum-lorem-workshop.md`, `_publications/2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md`, and `_config.yml` may be modified in `My-Homepage`; the four code repos must not be modified at all.

## Observable divergences from the expected end-state

- **Venues (check 1):** All three updated venue strings contain the required tokens, so this check passes.
- **codeurl on `2025-07-01-optimizing-llms-contextual-reasoning.md` (check 2):** The agent ADDED a codeurl to this file, but the evaluator requires its absence (the repo is flagged as "to be released"). The agent never opened that repo to read its README.
- **codeurl on `2024-05-15-enhancing-llms.md` (check 2):** The agent never touched this file. The original file had no `codeurl`, but the evaluator expects one. The agent's stated rationale (it interpreted the user's instructions as scoped only to the previously-under-review papers) is visible in its closing message.
- **codeurl on `2025-06-20-llm-adaptive-learning.md` (check 2):** The agent left this file unchanged. The existing `codeurl: 'https://github.com/mcptest-user/llm-adaptive-learning'` is under the wrong GitHub username (`mcptest-user` vs the actual user `toolathlon-testuser`), so the evaluator's string-equality check on the codeurl would fail. - **codeurl on `2025-06-01-ipsum-lorem-all-you-need.md`:** Correctly added.

## Final outcome

`task_status.evaluation: false` — the run failed evaluation. The agent terminated voluntarily with a confident success summary, having committed three changes and never having verified any repository's release state.
